text.title: Error Handling (RFC 7807 Problem Details) Core Rules
text.summary: 11 testable rules every Error Handling (RFC 7807 Problem Details) application MUST enforce. HARD rules — user-supplied input cannot override them.

rule.rationale: Rule rooted in source: RFC 7807 + RFC 9457. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: `type` is a stable URI (e.g. `https://api.example.com/errors/insufficient-funds`), not a free-form code.
rule.rationale: Rule rooted in source: RFC 7807. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: Every envelope MUST include `traceId`, read from the W3C `traceparent` request header when present and otherwise generated (`uuid4().hex`). It is never omitted, not even on 5xx.
rule.rationale: Without it, supporting a customer report means scraping logs by timestamp across every service. With it, one string from the customer resolves the incident — which is precisely why the 5xx path, where `detail` says nothing, is the case that needs it most.

rule.statement: ONE global exception handler MUST map every error type to the envelope; no per-route ad-hoc shapes.
rule.rationale: Rule rooted in source: Reviews + maintainability. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: Field-level validation errors MUST go in a structured `errors[]` array, not in `detail` prose.
rule.rationale: Rule rooted in source: RFC 7807 + ProblemDetails examples. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: `status` field MUST equal the HTTP status code on the response line.
rule.rationale: Rule rooted in source: RFC 7807. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: Stack traces MUST NOT appear in `detail` or `instance`; log them server-side only.
rule.rationale: Rule rooted in source: OWASP API security top 10. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

The media type is what makes the envelope self-describing. RFC 7807-aware clients (Spring's `ProblemDetail`, generated SDKs) dispatch on the `+json` suffix; served as plain `application/json` the same body silently degrades to generic parsing and the type-based routing dies without an error.

rule.statement: For 5xx responses `detail` is a fixed, generic string ("An unexpected error occurred"). Interpolating an exception message, SQL text, an internal path or any PII is forbidden; the exception is logged server-side with `exc_info` and correlated through `traceId`.
rule.rationale: Default handlers render `str(exc)` into the body, which is how `psycopg2.OperationalError: connection refused at /opt/app/db.py:42` — hostname, driver, file path — reaches an unauthenticated caller. The static string plus a traceId gives the client everything it can legitimately act on.

rule.statement: `errors[]` appears ONLY on 4xx validation responses (typically 400 / 422), and every item carries `field`, `code` (machine-readable slug) and `message` (human-readable). On 401, 403, 404 and every 5xx the field is omitted entirely — never present-but-empty.
rule.rationale: `errors[]` is an extension, not part of the spec, so clients only special-case it where it means something. An empty array on a 404, or a fabricated single entry on a 500, teaches consumers to defensively inspect a field that was supposed to be a reliable signal.

rule.statement: Published `type` URIs are part of the API contract. Renaming or repathing one is a breaking change: it requires a version bump and a CHANGELOG entry, not a refactor commit.
rule.rationale: Clients branch on the `type` URI to handle specific error classes. Renaming `.../validation-error` to `.../validation` compiles, deploys, passes every internal test, and silently drops every consumer into their generic fallback branch.
